items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.

items.summary: We present a synthesis of the Karimov–Alekberli (KA) Framework into a unified theory of Constitutional Intelligence: the capacity of an adaptive system to make consequential decisions that are simultaneously governed, explainable, accountable, reconstructable, verifiable, and capable of learning without retroactive falsification of the historical record. We formulate six formal results — one per required property — organized into three proof tiers: Tier A (two unconditional geometric results), Tier B (three conditional results valid under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), Tier C (one KA extension under a physical implementation assumption). Results draw on viability theory,information geometry, and thermodynamics. The theorems are organized in three tiers reflecting their current proof status: Tier A (fully proved geometric results), Tier B (conditional theorems under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), and Tier C (KA extensions requiring additional physical or topological conditions). A unifying condition, the Constitutional Integrity Criterion (CIC), is formulated as a representation theorem characterizing systems that satisfy all six properties simultaneously. We derive, under the CIC, that the governance loop Govern → Reason → Act → Remember → Learn → Govern defines a well-defined autonomous map on the constitutional moduli space that preserves the admissible region; fixed-point existence follows as a corollary under compactness. We position the framework within the existing literature on viability theory, formal verification, safe reinforcement learning, AI governance, and constitutional economics. We propose Constitutional Intelligence Science as the emerging discipline that unifies these results.
items.title: Constitutional Intelligence as Formal Science The Karimov–Alekberli Framework as Mathematical Foundation for Governed Institutional Cognition

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: A dictionary-first harmonisation tool for aligning constructs across five longitudinal youth-development cohorts — LSAC (Growing Up in Australia), ABCD, TESS (Trondheim Early Secure Study), Ten to Men and LSIC (Footprints in Time) — using variable-level metadata only, with no access to participant data and no redistribution of dictionary files. Cohorts and target constructs are configuration rather than code, so the tool generalises to constructs and cohorts beyond the anxiety application it was built for. Four adapters cover the dictionary shapes encountered, including inventories built from published documentation for cohorts with no custodian codebook; every row records the tier of evidence it rests on, distinguishing a custodian dictionary from a published cohort profile from a reconstruction assembled from methods sections. Outputs: a construct coverage matrix over primary waves; a register of constructs declared non-harmonisable, each with a mandatory stated reason and empirical confirmation of absence; an assessment, for every cohort pair, of whether genuine common items exist to anchor a multi-group latent model or whether the inference must be harmonised instead of the scale; a check that the cohorts holding a construct agree on who reported it; and an audit of published methodological claims against the cohorts' own dictionaries. Verdicts are evidence-tier aware. A cohort read from a custodian dictionary can contradict a claim; a cohort inventoried from publications can only fail to confirm one, and is reported as unverifiable rather than false. A declared absence is confirmed only for cohorts where a dictionary exists to confirm it in. Data governance is enforced in code rather than described in prose: a governed cohort is excluded unless explicitly included, its culturally grounded wellbeing indicators cannot be mapped as standing in for a diagnostic construct, and a non-harmonisable declaration without a stated reason raises an error. Provenance records a SHA-256 over every dictionary read, so a third party can confirm they ran against the same releases without those files being redistributed.

items.summary: Timely urban-canopy information is essential for linking remote sensing with heat, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture Imagery Program imagery (0.6 m RGB+NIR). DeepForest generated crown candidates; an NDVI threshold, non-maximum suppression, and box-prompted Segment Anything Model (ViT-B) produced a crown-anchored canopy surface. Analyses used the 25.92 km2 Census TIGER municipal boundary and a 100 m grid. The workflow retained 11,741 candidate crowns and mapped 7.71 km2 of canopy (29.8% of the city). On the identical extent, pixel precision was 0.804, pixel recall was 0.873, and 97.4% of candidate centers agreed with the 2022 USDA/CAL FIRE LiDAR-assisted canopy product (IoU 0.719; Dice 0.837; area recovery 108.5%). Approximately 49% of candidates occurred within 15 m of a road. Canopy was inversely associated with Landsat land-surface temperature (Spearman rho = -0.477; partial rho = -0.551 controlling for built probability), and spatial-lag modeling confirmed clear neighborhood structure. Two transparent attention surfaces combined canopy need with thermal and contextual indicators. The framework provides a reproducible, updateable screening layer that complements structural canopy products and municipal inventories while retaining assumptions, data provenance, and spatial diagnostics for planning interpretation.
items.title: From crown candidates to neighborhood screening: integrating optical GeoAI and spatial modeling for urban-canopy assessment in Davis, California

items.summary: Determinism and numerical reproducibility are increasingly required of GPU kernels in machine learning systems, yet deterministic implementations of the same kernel can still differ bit for bit. Floating-point reduction order is the primary cause, alongside partial-sum precision, fused multiply-add operations, and rounding placement. These choices may be hand-coded, selected by a block-level language such as Triton, or hidden inside a closed-source library such as cuBLAS or rocBLAS. A tile shape chosen for performance therefore also determines the arithmetic, potentially breaking batch invariance. Preserving a fixed order can cost up to 20 percent, while an autotuner cannot identify which configurations are bitwise equivalent. We characterize the factors determining the bitwise behavior of reductions and general matrix multiplication (GEMM). First, we introduce a descriptor of GEMM reduction order, including the partitioning of K in split-K GEMM. Using it, we perform the first black-box reconstruction of a closed-source library's arithmetic for bit-level correctness. Our family of Triton GEMMs matches NVIDIA cuBLAS in all tested cases on Blackwell and Hopper. For realistic LLM shapes with fused epilogues, it matches or exceeds torch.compile performance. Second, we enforce balanced-tree reduction during Triton lowering and introduce a data-layout optimization that brings 19 of 27 kernels on GB300 and H100 within 10 percent of free-order performance. Third, we develop sound static checkers for bitwise equivalence between compiled GPU kernels, including the first checker spanning NVIDIA PTX and AMD GCN. Integrated into Triton's autotuner, the checker restricts search to a single bit-equivalence class.
items.title: Taming Bitwise Behavior in GPU Kernels with Tensor Core: Black-Box Reconstruction, Compiler Enforcement, and Static Verification

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress, yet their massive storage and memory-bandwidth demands still hinder efficient deployment. Weight binarization is a promising solution, but existing binarization-based post-training quantization (PTQ) methods usually far exceed the nominal 1-bit storage target due to hidden overhead. To address this gap, we propose All for 1-Bit (AF1), a genuine 1-bit PTQ framework for LLMs. AF1 comprises two complementary components: (1) Null-space-Aware Binary Factorization (NABF) for improving binary reconstruction through Hessian-aware surrogate reparameterization, null-space-aware binary factorization, and scale-only global reconstruction; and (2) Hierarchical Shapley Allocation (HiSA) for assigning structural capacity using hierarchical Shapley sensitivity. Together, they preserve model accuracy under a strict 1.0-BPW budget in the PTQ setting. Experiments on LLaMA, Qwen, and Gemma families show that AF1 consistently outperforms existing binarization-based PTQ methods in perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Compared with BF16, AF1 achieves an average 2.5 times inference speedup and over 90% memory reduction across evaluated models, providing a practical path toward deployable genuine 1-bit compression for LLMs. The code for reproducibility is available at https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/AF1.
items.title: All for 1-Bit: Towards Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization for LLMs

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This first milestone is intentionally foundational. It establishes the formal structure needed for the later quantum-to-classical bridge without yet assuming the Schrödinger equation, Ehrenfest theorem, Newtonian dynamics, or the later Chronos connection. The next stage is to formalize quantum expectation values and their time evolution as the next step toward a machine-checked Ehrenfest bridge connecting accepted quantum mechanics with accepted classical physics. This deposit is part of an ongoing formal validation program. items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.

items.summary: Among the available anesthetic techniques, spinal anesthesia remains the preferred method for cesarean section procedures, because of its rapid onset and safety profile; however, it is frequently associated with hypotension that may compromise maternal and fetal stability. This study was conducted to assess the influence of lower limb elevation as a non-pharmacological intervention on blood pressure following spinal anesthesia. A one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design was implemented to evaluate 90 cesarean section patients who met the inclusion criteria. Blood pressure values, including systolic and diastolic parameters, were obtained at baseline and at the 5th, 10th, and 15th minutes after spinal anesthesia, and the data analysis using paired t-tests indicated significant increases in systolic and diastolic blood pressure over time, with mean systolic pressure rising from 87.59 mmHg to 97.89 mmHg and mean diastolic pressure increasing from 59.56 mmHg to 67.21 mmHg at minute 15 (p < 0.001). This study provides context-specific clinical evidence on the hemodynamic effects of lower limb elevation among post-spinal anesthesia cesarean section patients in a clinical setting. However, the non-inclusion of a control group and randomization reduce the strength of causal interpretation. These findings provide support for the notion that lower limb elevation may enhance potential benefits as a supportive intervention for post-spinal hypotension and warrant further controlled studies to confirm its efficacy.
items.title: Impact of lower limb elevation on blood pressure in cesarean patients: a quasi-experimental study

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.
items.title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content

items.summary: Agentic systems commit state-changing actions, but additional verifiers can inherit the same upstream fault. We present VP-CONTROL, a runtime-assurance design and deterministic benchmark for cost-aware commit gates. Its 48 task templates yield 2,880 scenarios across six fault regimes. A fixed-call 2 x 2 experiment separates verifier-model diversity from evidence-source diversity. On frozen proposals from two local actor families, a cross-model vote over shared evidence approves 62.9% of unsafe proposals, versus 22.9% with an independent source. The source effect is 40.9 percentage points, compared with 11.3 for model diversity. A portfolio controller selects verification plans using only deployment-observable metadata. Approximate cluster-adjusted calibration at a nominal 5% per-task target yields 1.9% unsafe execution and 38.2% automated safe coverage on the locked test. Matched-budget portfolios also improve on fixed verification policies. Transfer remains conditional: unseen fault families yield 16-26% risk, and a FinQA check fails to reproduce the source effect with the tested small verifiers. A preregistered live HTTP/SQLite study tests concurrent writes and lost responses. After-check races defeat verifier-only gates; transactional partial guards prevent only covered failures, while a full atomic guard records no unsafe effects across 216 episodes. Idempotent request identifiers prevent duplicate effects after lost responses. The results motivate explicit evidence lineage, cost-aware selection, and commit-time enforcement, while exposing the limits of approximate calibration and local-tool generalization.
items.title: Engineering Reliable Commit Gates for Agentic AI: Cost-Aware Verification Portfolios under Common-Mode Data Failures
